newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP warns of flat performance after review.
newsitem.headline: BHP warns of flat performance after review.

text.p: Resources giant The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Monday that trading conditions remained difficult and it expected a flat performance until it restructured and new projects were commissioned.

Announcing that it had completed a review of its future strategies, BHP said there would be a number of abnormal adjustments to its results for the year to May 31 due on June 28, and that some of these would have an adverse impact.
BHP said that after the completion of a strategic review it had re-affirmed its commitment to "superior performance and growth as measured against the performance of relevant peer group companies."

Managing Director John Prescott said in a statement there would be an increased focus on return on shareholder funds and that the performance of BHP's asset base, particularly those that were underperforming.
"As a result of this review, there will be a number of abnormal adjustments and these adjustments will be clarified in the release of BHP's full year result on 28 June," he said.
Prescott, in commenting on the fourth quarter results, said there would be some one-off items that would impact adversely on the results and trading conditions remained difficult.

"Given the assumptions regarding commodity prices it was expected that this situation would extend into next year with flat performance until the restructure takes greater effect and new projects are commissioned to contribute to earnings growth," he said.
Prescott said BHP's new projects woud provide a solid base for strong performance improvement over the medium term.
"BHP will continue with an aggressive growth strategy whilst at the same time seeking improved performance from its core assets to improve results," he said.

"The overall thrust of the company is to concentrate on our best performing businesses and new projects that can perform at high levels," he said. "We are committed to increasing our returns and to using our capital efficiently."
BHP shares fell 42 cents on the announcement after rising earlier to a new year high A$19.42 but the stock was down just six cents at A$19.26 in late morning trade.

The shares hit a 1997 low of A$16.45 on April 14 but had risen sharply since then as investors revalued the company on talk of a stronger world economy and after BHP announced a restructuring of its under-performing steel unit.

BHP reported a net profit of A$1.05 billion (US$808 million) for the year to May 31, 1996, down from A$1.22 billion a year earlier. For the nine months to February 28, net profit stood at A$1.17 billion, up from A$1.10 billion a year earlier.
